text: Ideas This memo outlines three distinct and actionable MVP (Minimum Viable Prod- uct) concepts designed to validate our core hypothesis for We b0nd in 1-2 weeks with a single developer. The goal is to move away from building a full-scale social media app and instead launch a targeted experiment to test the most critical assumption: that Latin American and European expats in New York desire to signal their social standing and connect with a curated, trusted circle of "friends of friends." Each idea is designed to be reductive, focusing on validating one specific aspect of this desire before we invest further in development. Group 1: Digital Identity & Social Signaling This group of ideas tests the desire for social signaling and belonging. The core concept is to create a digital artifact that users are proud to share, turning vanity and self-expression into our primary validation metric. Idea A: The "Digital Passport" • Concept: A single-page web app where a user designs their own "WeB0nd Expat Stamp" or "Digital Passport." This is a visually stunning, shareable badge representing their international identity. Users select high-signal affiliations like their origin city (e.g., "Madrid," "Rome"), their NYC anchor (e.g., "NYU," "Soho House"), and an emblem for a high-status hobby (e.g., polo, sailing, F1). • What It Validates: This directly tests the desire for social signaling. The key metric is the share rate to platforms like Instagram. It validates whether users will publicly align with the "higher-tiered society" brand we aim to build, and if the concept can spread virally within these exclusive circles. • MVP Plan (1 Week): – Tech: A simple front-end web app (Next.js on Vercel). – Backend: None required for V1. Use client-side image generation and local storage. 1 – Path to App: If successful, V2 adds QR codes for in-person scanning, which begins to build the social graph. Idea B: The "Digital Black Card" • Concept: A utility-driven status symbol. We partner with a single, high- status venue in NYC (e.g., an exclusive cocktail bar or gallery). The product is a minimalist app that functions as a digital membership card, offering a unique perk at that venue (e.g., a complimentary drink, skip- the-line access). The user shows their sleek, black "card" with a QR code, which the venue scans. • What It Validates: This tests real-world social signaling. Will users use a branded app in a public, high-status setting? It also validates our ability to form brand-aligned partnerships and tests if a tangible, real-world benefit drives adoption more effectively than purely digital features. • MVP Plan (1-2 Weeks): – Tech: A very simple native or progressive web app (PWA) to display a name and a dynamic QR code. A basic backend (Firebase/Supabase) manages the user list and validates scans. – Effort: The primary work is business development to secure the venue partnership. – Path to App: Every scan creates a data point of a user's presence at a specific location, building a graph based on verified, shared physical experiences. Group 2: Trust-Based Introduction Mechanics This group of ideas strips away all UI to test the absolute core of our "friends of friends" value proposition: the high-trust introduction. Idea C: "The Vouch Chain" • Concept: A gamified, invitation-only waitlist that becomes the product itself. You cannot join; you must be "vouched for" by an existing member. A new member receives a unique link to share with their trusted friends. When they vouch for someone, a new link in the chain is created. This builds the social graph from day one with zero social features. • What It Validates: This tests the power of exclusivity and social capital. Will users leverage their reputation to bring in friends? It measures our viral coefficient and the quality of the network, as we can trace the most influential "vouchers." • MVP Plan (1 Week): – Tech: A few simple web pages (Next.js on Vercel) and serverless functions to handle vouch requests and confirmations, potentially via SMS (Twilio). 2 – Backend: A simple Firestore or Supabase database to store members and their vouch status. – Path to App: The vouch chain is the initial social graph. The full app is then launched to this pre-vetted, interconnected user base. Idea D: The "Inner Circle" Bot • Concept: A white-glove, "human-in-the-loop" introduction service run via a WhatsApp or Telegram bot. A user "applies" by answering key questions and naming a mutual friend who can vouch for them. Our team then manually reviews the applications (in a simple Google Sheet) and, upon finding a match, creates a private group chat introducing the two new users and their mutual friend. • What It Validates: This tests the raw value of a high-quality, curated introduction. It removes all technical complexity to answer: Is this service valuable enough for people to engage? It provides direct feedback on the quality of our "matches." • MVP Plan (1 Week): – Tech: A landing page (Carrd/Webflow), a bot (ManyChat/Twilio script), and a Google Sheet or Airtable as the database. The "backend" is the founding team. – Path to App: This manual process builds a high-fidelity social graph of verified, successful introductions. The app is then built to automate and scale this proven process. Group 3: Community & Place-Based Discovery This idea focuses on validating the "bubble" by creating a sense of shared identity and insider knowledge around physical locations. Idea E: "The Nomad's Atlas" • Concept: A private, members-only interactive map of New York. Instead of showing people, the map shows anonymous "moments" or "insider tips" pinned by other members (e.g., "Best old fashioned at this speakeasy," "Spontaneous rooftop party here"). The only way to interact is to contribute your own pins. A pin might have context like, "Pinned by a friend of Alexandra's," creating intrigue without revealing identities. • What It Validates: This tests the desire for a shared "insider" identity. Are users willing to contribute their knowledge to a collective resource? It validates if the "friend of a friend" context makes a recommendation more powerful than a generic review. • MVP Plan (1-2 Weeks): – Tech: A web-based map using Mapbox or Leaflet. 3 – Backend: Firebase/Supabase with geo-query capabilities to store and retrieve pins. Simple user authentication is required. – Path to App: User contributions and interactions (e.g., upvoting a pin) create the initial data points for the social graph. V2 could add a "check-in" feature to create connections based on shared presence. 4
